name: Amara Bissap-Tamarind Sour
description: A sharp, lip-puckering blend of synth-bissap and tamarind extract with a salted rim finish. Popular with street vendors in Tier 2 markets who serve it over crushed ice.
flavor_profile: Deep hibiscus tartness upfront, followed by a slow tamarind pull and a faint salt-mineral finish. Medium carbonation with a dry aftertaste.
cultural_context: Amara Bissap-Tamarind Sour has a cult following among Shelf workers who drink it chilled after night shifts. The salt finish is rumored to have been an accident in the original batch that the brand kept deliberately.
story_hooks: A Shelf vendor has been selling this soda for 20 years from the same corner — he claims the original formula is different from what Amara Bottling now sells, and he has the last case of the original run.
A Tier 4 food journalist is writing a piece on Shelf food culture and becomes obsessed with this drink, drawing corporate attention to Amara's unregistered distribution network.
Two gangs in Tier 1 have an unspoken truce rule: deals happen when both parties are holding an Amara Sour. Breaking the rule has consequences.
